newsitem.title: USA: MONSANTO, DEKALB SAY GMO CORN NO PLANT PEST RISK.
newsitem.headline: MONSANTO, DEKALB SAY GMO CORN NO PLANT PEST RISK.

text.p: Monsanto Co and Dekalb Genetics Corp have asked the U.S. Agriculture Department to grant nonregulated status for genetically engineered corn known as GA21, the USDA said on Wednesday.
In a Federal Register notice, the agency's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said the strain of corn had been genetically engineered for tolerance to the herbicide glyphosate.
The USDA said it would accept public comments until Oct. 14 on whether the new corn line presents a plant pest risk.

Monsanto and Dekalb said in a petition to the USDA that the corn line should not be regulated by APHIS because it does not present a plant pest risk. The corn has been engineered to to tolerate the active ingredient in the herbicide Roundup.
The corn line has been evaluated in field trials conducted since 1994 under APHIS.
